questions.q: In script mode, where should your training script save the trained model so SageMaker uploads it to S3?
options: Directly to an S3 bucket using boto3 inside the script
The current working directory of the notebook
The folder named by the SM_MODEL_DIR environment variable (/opt/ml/model)
The folder named by SM_CHANNEL_TRAIN
questions.explain: SageMaker compresses whatever is in the model folder (/opt/ml/model, exposed as SM_MODEL_DIR) into model.tar.gz and uploads it to the job's S3 output path.

questions.q: How do hyperparameters reach a script-mode training script?
options: As command-line arguments the script can read with argparse
They are hard-coded into the container image
They are written back to the notebook as variables
They are read from the model.tar.gz file
questions.explain: The SDK passes the hyperparameters dictionary to the script as command-line arguments, which argparse parses.

questions.q: Why give environment-variable arguments a local default such as os.environ.get("SM_MODEL_DIR", "./model")?
options: SageMaker refuses to run scripts without a default
So the same script runs unchanged on your own machine for testing
Defaults make the training job cheaper
Defaults are needed to enable spot training
questions.explain: Locally the variables do not exist, so the defaults let you debug the exact script for free before paying for a cloud run.

options: Sets how long the endpoint stays up after training
Limits how fast the script can read S3 data
Controls how many trials a tuning job runs
Ends a job that runs too long, first sending SIGTERM so the script can save
questions.explain: It caps the runtime to control cost. SageMaker sends SIGTERM and allows a grace period of 120 seconds before forcibly stopping.

questions.q: A scikit-learn model was trained and pickled with joblib in one container version. What is the safest practice for hosting it?
options: Host it with an older scikit-learn to save memory
Use the same scikit-learn version for training and hosting
Convert it to CSV first
Hosting versions never matter for joblib files
questions.explain: A joblib file is a pickle of the library's objects, so loading it with a different scikit-learn version can fail or behave differently.
